significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that an LLM can encode a set's members and cardinality before answering, while emitting one member causally suppresses the retrieval signals of remaining members and promotes premature stopping; this is a form-(iii) predictive coupling backed by a form-(ii) causal decomposition, rather than merely an existence claim. The claim would establish both the phenomenon that "the set's true cardinality and unemitted members are partially decodable" and a mechanism in which "emitted-member directions suppress the retrieval directions of remaining members," thereby distinguishing missing knowledge, member inhibition, and stop control as explanations for separate enumeration failures; this would materially refine staged factual-recall accounts such as Geva et al. (2023). Verified-false and verified-true are distinguishable: failure of the stipulated latent-membership and inhibition relationships would rule out this specific serialization-bottleneck account, although it would not by itself identify the alternative mechanism. In the topic-substitution check, the broad topic of knowledge representation would not earn this score; the set-specific ordering, predictive coupling, and decomposition of omission versus early stopping are the above-median contribution.

reach.justification: The claim names three usable handles: a decoded "set signature," "emitted-member suppression removal," and "set-cardinality-aware stop calibration." The latter two are ex ante decode-time controls because they act before the next omission or premature EOS, leaving an action window rather than merely explaining an already completed failure. Although their activation directions would need re-extraction for each model, the asserted relation—emitting members suppresses remaining-member retrieval and predicts omission—would still predict what to look for across the claimed finite-set categories and LLM families; likely downstream users include interpretability researchers and practitioners building or auditing systems that must enumerate complete lists. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: generic knowledge-retrieval research supplies no comparable pre-failure intervention, while the quoted suppression-removal and stopping controls do, though their narrow finite-set scope and model-internal calibration keep reach below the top band.
